title: Collection Design and Performance
subtopics: Time and Space Complexity of Common Operations
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of collection design and performance using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates collection design and performance.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Collection Design and Performance** as part of **Strings, Arrays, and Collections**. Select a collection by the invariants you need—ordering, uniqueness, key lookup, or indexed access—and check the cost of transformations. Use the subtopics—Lists Versus Sets Versus Maps, Choosing Mutable or Read-Only Types, Time and Space Complexity of Common Operations—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Functions, null safety, strings, and collections are the building blocks of most practical Kotlin code. Choosing the right operation reduces avoidable errors and makes behavior easier to test.

items.title: Lists Versus Sets Versus Maps
items.text: Lists Versus Sets Versus Maps is best learned by tracing a small collection before and after the operation. Check ordering, duplicate handling, empty inputs, and whether the API returns a new value or mutates a mutable receiver.

items.title: Choosing Mutable or Read-Only Types
items.text: Choosing Mutable or Read-Only Types is one part of collection design and performance. Connect its definition to the example, identify the input/state it changes, and verify the expected behavior with a small test case.

items.title: Time and Space Complexity of Common Operations
items.text: Time and Space Complexity of Common Operations should be evaluated against input size, allocation behavior, and workload. Start with a correctness test and reproducible measurement; choose the simplest implementation that meets the requirement.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake to avoid
content_blocks.text: A read-only collection reference proves that no code can mutate the underlying data.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset

Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
